title: Regularized barycentric Rényi divergences
abstract: Barycentric Rényi divergences were introduced in [Mosonyi, Bunth, Vrana, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024] as an alternative to standard Kubo-Ando constructions to define multivariate quantum Rényi divergences. They are defined via a variational expression and depend on a finite collection of quantum relative entropies $D^{q_x}$. When all the relative entropies are monotone under CPTP maps then so are the corresponding barycentric Rényi divergences, and when all the relative entropies are additive then the corresponding barycentric Rényi divergences are subadditive under tensor product. Additivity has only been established before for the case where all $D^{q_x}$ are chosen to be the Umegaki relative entropy, which is also the only case where the barycentric Rényi divergence (called the minimal one) admits an explicit expression.   Here we settle the problem of additivity by showing that for any choice of additive and monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric Rényi divergence coincides with the minimal barycentric Rényi divergence on strictly positive inputs. This in turn implies that the only additive barycentric Rényi divergence is the minimal one.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes barycentric Rényi divergences, which are generalizations of quantum relative entropy for multiple quantum states. The authors solve the long-standing additivity problem by proving that the only quantum relative entropy structure that allows for additivity is the minimal one derived from the Umegaki relative entropy. This provides a powerful tool for quantifying multi-partite quantum correlations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the definition and additivity properties of multivariate quantum Rényi divergences, specifically the barycentric Rényi divergence.
main_result: It proves that for any choice of additive and monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric Rényi divergence must coincide with the minimal (Umegaki) one on strictly positive inputs, implying the minimal one is the unique additive choice.
method: The analysis involves defining the divergence via variational expressions and comparing different forms (e.g., $D_{\max}$ vs $D_{	ext{Um}}$) using tensor product structures and regularization techniques.
model_or_system: The study is set in the context of quantum information theory, dealing with collections of positive semi-definite operators $W = (W_x)_{x \in X}$ acting on a Hilbert space $H$.
key_observables: Barycentric Rényi divergences ($D_{b,q}^P(W)$), the regularized divergence ($\mathcal{D}_{b,q}^P(W)$), and the quantum relative entropy ($D_q$).
important_parameters: The probability distribution $P$ over the index set $X$, and the choice of the quantum relative entropy $D_q$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the relative entropies $D_q$ are monotone and that the inputs are strictly positive for the final additivity result.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the divergence, establishing inequalities between different forms ($D_{b,Um}^P \le D_{b,q}^P \le D_{b,max}^P$), and culminating in the proof that the additivity property forces the divergence to be the minimal Umegaki form.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework developed for characterizing divergences is fundamental for quantifying distinguishability between quantum states, which is crucial for quantum channel capacity and resource theories.
